english.note: Use 淨係 as the all-purpose choice for “only” or “merely,” including a deliberately low-key “just.”
This is the all-purpose spoken choice for excluding others or limiting the amount to a stated number.
Use this for “simply” meaning only or merely, including when it means alone or without anything added.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that something is only or just the case.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that only one thing, person, or material is involved.
Use this when entirely means only or solely, excluding everyone or everything else.
Use this for the limited-scope meaning ‘only’ or ‘just’, rather than for following rules strictly.
Use 淨係 for ordinary “only” or “exclusively,” including when highlighting a selected subset such as blazers alone.
